def: A torsion balance used for measuring electric attraction orrepulsion.
Sloping gradually; shelving.The shore was shelving and shallow. Shak.
A Hebrew measure of liquids, containing three quarts, one pint,one gill, English measure. W. H. Ward.
Relating to the binding of books. [R.]
A person who has the care of neat cattle; a cowherd. Dryden.
A pie made of truffles, much esteemed by epicures.
The doctrine of signs as the expression of thought orreasoning; the science of indicating thought by signs. Smart.
The state of being putrescent; putrescent matter.
Of or pertaining to the colleterium of insects. R. Owen.

A tropical plant (Ananassa sativa); also, its fruit; -- socalled from the resemblance of the latter, in shape and externalappearance, to the cone of the pine tree. Its origin is unknown,though conjectured to be American.
